summary: Mirza-ye Qomi, born Mirza Abolghasem Gilani in 1739 in Japelaq, Iran, was a Shiite jurist and religious authority during the reign of Fath Ali Shah Qajar. He is best known for Qawanin al-Usul, written in 1791, which was a leading seminary textbook on the principles of Islamic jurisprudence for more than forty years. He studied with his father, then in Khansar, and then in Karbala under Muhammad Baqir Behbahani, who authorised him to practise ijtihad. He later settled in Qom and soon became its leading Shiite authority. Under him, the Qom seminary overshadowed the seminary of Isfahan. He trained many prominent scholars and wrote on law, theology and other subjects. He was also a poet and calligrapher. He died in 1815 and is buried in Qom.
